issue.title: Music.OnCompletionListener does not call when the length of the Music is 0.

body: Created a test, using a WAV with 5000 samples at 44.1khz. Couldn't reproduce this on the desktop. Couldn't download the file @EyeOfMidas provided. Will reopen if you can provide the file and the issue is reproduceable.

I use openSUSE 13.1 and I've the same issue with latest libGDX 1.0.1
This file doesn't work:
http://www.contezero.com/libgdx/tic.ogg
The same file with the addition of 300ms of silence at the end plays correctly:
 http://www.contezero.com/libgdx/tic_long.ogg

Confirm @ConteZero's post.
Latest libgdx sources, lwjgl, Win7x64.

I tried it with that tic.ogg on Windows 8. It did not play. I loaded into Audacity and re-exported without  modifications and it works. This suggests that the original file is in some way not compatible with the version of Jorbis that libgdx uses (which is the latest version).

Well, did some more debugging. If I reduce the buffer size in [OggInputStream.java](https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/blob/master/backends/gdx-backend-lwjgl/src/com/badlogic/gdx/backends/lwjgl/audio/OggInputStream.java) to 512, the original tic.ogg works.

The good news: was able to reproduce it! Thanks for providing the files.

The bad news: it's a bug in the ogg decoder we use on the desktop (JLayer). http://libgdx.badlogicgames.com/uploads/Screen%20Shot%202014-05-10%20at%2021.45.51-2B8le2VSur.png it thinks there's no audio data in that short OGG and returns 0 PCM data. I'll dig a bit deeper, but don't hold your breath.
@MobiDevelop is the hero we don't deserve. Fixed this according to his discovery.
Now its the issue the other way round. If the block size of the OGG file is too large (and that is possible as a OGG page is allowed to be up to 64kb large) the entire game loop crashes.

Yes, yes, we hear. Open an issue, post a problematic audio file. Please
